cards.title: Practical Considerations for the Design, Conduct, and Reporting of Clinical Pharmacokinetic Drug-Drug Interaction Studies in Drug Development.
cards.what: Clinical pharmacokinetic drug-drug interaction (PK-DDI) studies are frequently required in drug development when metabolizing enzymes and transporters determine pharmacokinetics. Drugs can be victims, perpetrators, or victims and perpetrators, of PK-DDIs, so the clinical consequences of these interactions, particularly the risks of severe adverse effects and therapeutic failures leading to poor clinical outcomes, must be well understood prior to regulatory filings.
cards.original_title: Practical Considerations for the Design, Conduct, and Reporting of Clinical Pharmacokinetic Drug-Drug Interaction Studies in Drug Development.

cards.title: Evaluation of Therapeutic Drug Monitoring for Vancomycin with Ratio of Area Under the Curve to Minimum Inhibitory Concentration at a Children's and Women's Tertiary Hospital.
cards.what: Guidelines for therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) of vancomycin recommend monitoring the ratio of area under the curve to minimum inhibitory concentration (AUC/MIC), with a target of 400-600 for both adults and children, rather than trough-based monitoring. AUC/MIC-based TDM for vancomycin was implemented at the study centre in April 2021.
cards.source: PubMed, The Canadian journal of hospital pharmacy
cards.original_title: Evaluation of Therapeutic Drug Monitoring for Vancomycin with Ratio of Area Under the Curve to Minimum Inhibitory Concentration at a Children's and Women's Tertiary Hospital.
